clue.text: Greek character is out to avenge, first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A character in Greek drama is bent on revenge above everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Grass playing well before being cut

parts.note: a sportsman playing well is in form

indicators.note: being cut says the word for before loses its final letter

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A lawn kept in fine condition before mowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is the slang verb and noun for informing on someone, not the lawn the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass is British slang for a police informer, someone who tells on criminals.

clue.text: All but one in football team fit and sound?

parts.words: All but one in football team
parts.note: a football team has eleven players, so all but one is ten
fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: Nearly every player in a football side is fit and healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable argument is a sound one, capable of being defended or held.

clue.text: All the runners in line

definitions.meaning: first meaning: every competitor in a race, collectively
second meaning: a line of work or area of expertise

explanation.definitionFit: The field is the whole set of entrants in a race, and one's field is one's line of business or study.

clue.text: Cross court as if suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry court treats evidence as if it were dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractious means irritable and quarrelsome, an angry, cross temperament.

clue.text: Back where witch lived? She eschews hotel

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is the medium consulted by Saul in the Bible

indicators.note: eschews means avoids, so the hotel letter is left out of the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about a witch's former home, and a woman who avoids staying at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a plan is to support it, which is what endorsing it means.

clue.text: Order to carry out, endlessly creamy?

parts.note: to do something is to carry it out

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for creamy loses its last letter

parts.note: creamy food is rich

explanation.surface: A command to remove something that is never-endingly creamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command but is an architectural order of columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, with plain, sturdy columns.

clue.text: When to return iron box holding valuables

indicators.note: to return asks for the word for when to be read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Instructions on when to give back an iron strongbox full of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a strong lockable cabinet where money and precious items are kept.

clue.text: Harvester parked on road? People won't take this well

indicators.note: parked on says the harvesting tool sits on top of the road abbreviation, before it in this down answer

parts.note: a sickle is a curved blade used for harvesting crops
AVE, short for avenue, is a kind of road

explanation.surface: A combine harvester left on the road; people won't take kindly to that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like 'kindly', but it means in good health: this is leave taken when unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick leave is time off granted to employees who are ill, so the healthy do not use it.

clue.text: Wiggling of toe is flirtatious activity

indicators.note: wiggling means moving about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Waggling one's toe is a form of flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing footsie is touching someone's feet under the table as a flirtatious game.

clue.text: Is it the boss we must see when someone's late?

definitions.text: Is it the boss we must see when someone's late?

parts.words: Is it the boss we must see when someone's late?
parts.note: late here means dead, not tardy, so the person to see runs the burial arrangements

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a manager dealing with an employee who turns up late; 'late' really means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker directs the arrangements once someone has died, the late person of the clue.

clue.text: Sort of stew and batter to conclude the order?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stew made with the meat of a ...
second meaning: in cricket slang a ... is a hopeless batter who comes in at the end of the batting order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' and 'stew' suggest cooking, but the batter is a cricketer; a 'rabbit' is a tail-end player who cannot bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit stew is a traditional dish, and cricket calls an inept last-in batsman a rabbit.

clue.text: Disregarding dangers in bay around Kuala Lumpur?

indicators.note: around says the word for bay surrounds the letters for the Malaysian capital

parts.note: a bay is an alcove or recess in a wall

explanation.surface: Someone ignoring peril while sailing in a bay near the Malaysian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless person acts heedlessly, paying no attention to risk.

clue.text: Need coat repaired — there's yarn

indicators.note: repaired implies the letters of the two words are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A coat needs mending, and there is yarn for the darning.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a story, and an anecdote is a short entertaining account of an incident.

clue.text: Naval officer has something to go on, gathering men

indicators.note: gathering says the word for the chair collects the letters for men inside it

parts.note: a commode is a chair containing a chamber pot, something to go on when needing the toilet
OR, other ranks, means soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A naval officer has a pretext for proceeding, rallying the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodore is a naval rank above captain and below rear admiral.

clue.text: Chap grabbing old news boss made complaint

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for chap takes hold of the letter for old inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man
ED, short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A man seizing an elderly newspaper editor caused a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to grumble or complain, so 'made complaint' is its past tense.

clue.text: Heavy metal god not entirely covered with hair

indicators.note: covered with says the word for hair goes round the shortened god

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

indicators.note: not entirely says the god's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Ganesh is the elephant-headed Hindu god

explanation.surface: A heavy metal rocker idolised, half hidden under a mane of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests long-haired rock, but it is a dense chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a hard, dense transition element, a heavy metal in the chemical sense.

clue.text: Check blunder in endless easing of international tension

indicators.note: in says the word for blunder goes inside the shortened word
endless says the word for easing of tension loses its last letter

parts.note: détente is the relaxing of strained relations between nations
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A mistake halts an ongoing thaw in international relations.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent checks or discourages action, as nuclear weapons were meant to.

clue.text: Not wild about hour taken by southern river

indicators.note: taken by says the abbreviation for southern is attached to what comes before it
about says the word for not wild goes round the abbreviation for hour

parts.note: not wild means tame

explanation.surface: Someone unexcited about a southern river trip lasting an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river flowing through London to the North Sea.

clue.text: She's writer looking run down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: H. Rider ... wrote the novel She
second meaning: worn out and gaunt

explanation.walkthrough: 'She' looks like a pronoun but is the title of an 1887 adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard wrote She, and a haggard face is drawn and exhausted-looking.

clue.text: Showing disrespect, two things swindlers do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: scorn, the disdain shown towards someone
second meaning, read cryptically: swindlers con and tempt their victims, and those two verbs run together make the word

explanation.surface: A conman's disdain for his marks shows in the two tricks of his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The two things are CON and TEMPT, written one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn, the attitude shown when one treats someone with disdain.

clue.text: Shy target one among lovely bunch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at a fair, a ... shy is a stall where balls are thrown to knock ... off stands
second meaning: from the song 'I've Got a Lovely Bunch of ...'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like bashful but is a throw; a coconut shy is a British fairground game.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground shy's targets are nuts, and the music-hall song celebrates a lovely bunch of them.

clue.text: Despondency shown by south-east Asians in speech?

indicators.note: in speech says the word for these people is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Malays are people of Malaysia and the Malay peninsula

explanation.surface: Low spirits shown by people from south-east Asia when talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease or low spirits, a gloomy listlessness.

clue.text: Sceptic coasting at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or lost, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doubter drifting along the shoreline in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that God's existence can be known, a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Wartime boffin abandons grand Italian location

indicators.note: abandons says the letter for grand is dropped from the scientist's name

parts.note: Alan Turing, the codebreaker at Bletchley Park in the Second World War; boffin is British slang for a scientist
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A wartime scientist leaves a magnificent spot in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in Piedmont, north-west Italy, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Yearly projection from Fremantle retailers

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: A sales forecast for the year from shops in the Australian port of Fremantle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yearly projection' looks like a business forecast; it is a deer's bony growth, shed and regrown every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer grow and shed an antler annually, and it is a branched bony outgrowth from the head.

clue.text: Area in vibrant venue in Bristol needing many workers?

indicators.note: in says the letter for area is placed inside the rearranged letters
vibrant means quivering and lively, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A lively music venue somewhere in Bristol takes plenty of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vibrant' shakes up VENUE IN BRISTOL, and the A for 'Area' goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is labour-intensive requires a large workforce relative to the capital involved.

clue.text: Hardcore band, unconvincing here, finally shows bite

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A hardcore punk band, weak in this gig, at last shows some attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge and bite both mean sharpness or incisiveness, as in a voice or performance.

clue.text: Money returned on explosive component

indicators.note: returned means the slang word for money is read backwards

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Cash was given back on the strength of an explosive part.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, is potassium nitrate, the oxidising ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Ecstasy in club for pound

indicators.note: in says the letter for ecstasy goes inside the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Taking ecstasy at a nightclub in exchange for a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat and to pound both mean to strike repeatedly and hard.
